Question: A 7-year-old male patient presents for his recall appointment. His mother reports that he frequently forgets to brush his teeth at night and consumes several sugary snacks daily. Clinical examination reveals early demineralization on several posterior teeth. What is the MOST appropriate primary preventive measure to recommend for this patient?
Explanation: While sealants (option A) and fluoride applications (options C, D) are important preventive measures, addressing the root causes of caries risk through dietary counseling and reinforcing proper oral hygiene techniques (brushing, flossing) is the fundamental and most appropriate primary preventive measure. Without these foundational changes, other interventions may have limited long-term success.
